strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem in self-supervised audio representation learning: the evaluation gap between fine-tuning and frozen feature probing, as well as reproducibility challenges in recent state-of-the-art baselines.

The proposed Convex Gated Probing (CGP) offers an effective, parameter-efficient evaluation protocol that significantly narrows the gap between frozen probing and end-to-end fine-tuning without modifying the backbone architecture.

Provides insightful diagnostic analysis on the layer-wise distribution of semantic information, demonstrating both quantitatively and qualitatively how decoder capacity and attention gating shift high-level abstractions toward later encoder blocks.
Systematic and transparent ablation studies isolate the individual contributions of the data frontend, attention gating for target generation, and decoder architecture.

Demonstrates strong frozen-probing performance across multiple audio classification benchmarks (AudioSet, ESC-50, Speech Commands V2), outperforming prior probing methodologies by substantial margins.
weaknesses: While the authors convincingly document reproduction discrepancies with prior published numbers for SSLAM, the downstream fine-tuning performance of BAT on AS-2M (48.55 mAP) still trails the previously claimed literature baseline of 50.2 mAP.

The core architectural components of BAT (e.g., gated attention from recent language modeling work, larger ViT decoders from MAE, and local min-max spectrogram normalization) represent an integration of known techniques rather than fundamentally new conceptual mechanisms.

Probing with 10,000 prototypes and layer-wise soft gating introduces non-trivial auxiliary parameters and optimization overhead compared to traditional linear probing, placing CGP closer to parameter-efficient transfer learning than minimal representation probing.
The paper lacks detailed computational efficiency metrics (such as wall-clock runtime, memory footprint, or FLOPs) comparing CGP evaluation against standard linear probing and full fine-tuning.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem in audio self-supervised learning, specifically the heavy reliance on fragile fine-tuning recipes and the lack of faithful, reproducible probing protocols.

Convex Gated Probing (CGP) offers an effective parameter-efficient approach to evaluate frozen representations across Transformer layers, bridging much of the observed gap between linear probing and full fine-tuning.

Provides a thorough and methodical ablation of key pre-training components, demonstrating clear empirical benefits from local spectrogram normalization, attention gating, and increased decoder expressiveness.
The layer-wise representation analysis offers valuable empirical insight into how decoder capacity alters the semantic information bottleneck across the depth of the encoder.
weaknesses: The core individual design components are primarily adaptations of prior techniques (e.g., attention gating from recent language modeling work, expressive decoders from masked autoencoding, and prototypical pooling from earlier audio probing literature), making the conceptual novelty somewhat modular.

Although the authors demonstrate improvements over their reproduced versions of prior baselines under controlled settings, the fine-tuned results on AudioSet-2M still do not exceed the highest self-reported baseline figures in the existing literature.
The computational cost and training overhead of maintaining and optimizing 10,000 prototypes for probing are not thoroughly analyzed or compared against standard linear probe training runtimes.

Downstream validation is confined to standard sound classification and keyword spotting benchmarks; evaluating on diverse tasks such as audio retrieval, sound event localization, or bioacoustics would provide broader support for the representations' generalizability.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental evaluation issue in audio self-supervised learning: downstream fine-tuning obscures the intrinsic quality of representations and introduces reproducibility bottlenecks, while standard linear probing significantly underestimates model capacity.

Convex Gated Probing (CGP) provides an effective and computationally tractable middle ground between rigid linear probes and full fine-tuning by combining learnable layer-wise convex gating with prototype-based token similarity pooling.

Provides a valuable reproducibility critique of recent audio SSL models (such as EAT and SSLAM), identifying fragile loss-scaling heuristics and undocumented engineering quirks within legacy codebases.

The proposed architectural refinements in BAT—specifically local min-max input normalization, attention gating to enable end-of-block targets without collapse, and deeper ViT decoders—are theoretically grounded and well validated through systematic ablations.
The layer-wise representation analysis (Figure 4) offers clear mechanistic insights into how decoder capacity shifts semantic information toward deeper encoder layers.
weaknesses: Although BAT convincingly beats the reproduced baselines under identical standardized training recipes, its fine-tuned AS-2M performance (48.55 mAP) does not match the peak numbers reported in the original SSLAM publication (50.2 mAP), warranting further discussion on whether this discrepancy stems from dataset variance, unlabeled data access, or hyperparameter sweeps.

CGP relies on optimizing a relatively large number of prototypes (10,000 vectors), which adds non-trivial memory and optimization overhead during evaluation compared to standard linear probing, even if it remains cheaper than fine-tuning.

Evaluation is restricted to standard sound event classification and speech recognition benchmarks (AudioSet, ESC-50, Speech Commands); extending evaluation to broader downstream domains such as bioacoustics, music information retrieval, or HEAR tasks would further substantiate general audio representation claims.

strengths: Thorough critical evaluation and demystification of recent audio SSL SOTA (EAT, SSLAM), exposing fragile finetuning practices, undocumented training heuristics (such as 80,000x loss scaling), and reproducibility issues.

Well-motivated and effective probing technique (CGP) that addresses the spatial and hierarchical bottlenecks of ViT representations by combining prototype-based patch pooling with learnable convex layer weighting.

Systematic and clear ablative analysis of architectural and pretraining choices, successfully demonstrating how audio frontend normalization, gated attention, and decoder capacity shift semantic representations to the deeper layers of the encoder.

Comprehensive downstream evaluation spanning diverse audio domains and tasks, including AudioSet (20k/2M), ESC-50, Speech Commands v2, DCASE Sound Event Detection, bioacoustic domain shift (BirdSet HSN), and LibriSpeech ASR.
weaknesses: Several core technical components are direct adaptations of recent external ideas (e.g., attention gating from Qiu et al. (2025), frontend normalization from Ghaffari & Devos (2024), scaling MIM decoders from He et al. (2022), and prototype pooling from Rauch et al. (2026)), making the algorithmic novelty incremental.

With 10,000 prototypes and 3K similarity features per sample, CGP introduces significant parameter overhead (23.49M parameters for AudioSet compared to 0.41M for standard linear probes), blurring the distinction between a minimal diagnostic probe and a parameter-efficient adaptation head.

The paper does not reach the previously claimed AudioSet-2M finetuning ceiling of 50.2 mAP from SSLAM, and while the authors provide justifiable evidence that SSLAM is not reproducible under standard protocols, further discussion on the exact source of this gap would strengthen the narrative.

strengths: The paper tackles a critical and timely issue in audio self-supervised learning (SSL): the heavy reliance on fragile full-model finetuning and the presence of undocumented heuristics and reproducibility gaps in recent state-of-the-art models (such as EAT and SSLAM).

Convex Gated Probing (CGP) offers an effective, layer-aware probing mechanism that substantially bridges the gap between frozen-feature evaluation and full finetuning, outperforming previous probing strategies like ProtoBin, VQT, and Head2Toe while maintaining low latency.

The methodological improvements in BAT are systematically ablated and well-grounded: modernizing the frontend to local min-max normalization, incorporating gated attention to unlock End-of-Block targets, and deepening the decoder to shift semantic representation toward later encoder layers.

The experimental evaluation is exceptionally comprehensive, spanning standard audio classification (AudioSet, ESC-50), speech recognition (LibriSpeech), speech classification (Speech Commands), sound event detection (SED), and out-of-distribution evaluation (BirdSet-HSN), across multiple probing paradigms.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty of individual components is somewhat incremental; CGP primarily integrates scalar layer-weighting (common in speech benchmarks like SUPERB) with prototype probing (ProtoBin), and the architectural modifications (attention gating, larger ViT decoders) adapt established ideas from vision and NLP.

The probing head in CGP is heavily parameterized, requiring 10,000 prototypes (over 23M parameters for AudioSet), which borders on training a substantial adaptation model rather than a lightweight probe, even though the backbone remains frozen.

While the paper convincingly demonstrates superior performance over fair reproductions of prior methods, BAT's AS-2M finetuning score (48.85 mAP) still falls short of the highest self-reported numbers in SSLAM (50.2 mAP), which may leave questions about whether specific hyperparameter regimes or undocumented tricks in prior baselines were fully matched.

strengths: Important problem and timely motivation: Audio SSL research has increasingly relied on complex end-to-end finetuning recipes on AudioSet that obscure whether performance gains stem from better SSL representations or hyperparameter tuning/optimization artifacts. The paper tackles this issue head-on with both evaluation and modeling contributions.

Methodologically sound probing protocol: Convex Gated Probing (CGP) offers an effective layer-aware, prototype-based frozen evaluation mechanism. As demonstrated across extensive benchmarks, CGP substantially closes the gap between frozen probing and full finetuning (e.g., reaching 45.03 mAP on AS-2M compared to 31.19 mAP with linear probing and 48.85 mAP with finetuning).

Insightful analysis of representation dynamics: The analysis of layer-wise semantic peaks (Figure 4 and Figure 6) clearly illustrates how decoder capacity and attention gating affect encoder representations in Masked Latent Regression (MLR), shifting semantic information toward later blocks and correlating strongly with learned layer gating weights.

Systematic and reproducible pretraining design: BAT systematically improves upon the legacy fairseq/D2V2 codebase by introducing local min-max frontend normalization, gated attention to stabilize End-of-Block regression targets, and removing unstable heuristic loss scaling factors (e.g., 8e4 global loss weights).

Comprehensive experimental validation: The paper tests across diverse downstream tasks including multi-label audio classification (AudioSet-2M/20k), environmental sound classification (ESC-50), keyword spotting (Speech Commands v2), sound event detection (DCASE 2016 Task 2), out-of-distribution bioacoustics (BirdSet HSN), and speech recognition (LibriSpeech), benchmarking against multiple probing methods (LP, LCGP, PB, VQT, H2T) and model architectures.
weaknesses: Incremental individual algorithmic novelties: While the collective modernization and empirical execution are strong, the individual components are largely adaptations of existing ideas: CGP combines soft layer-weighting (common in speech benchmarks like SUPERB) with prototypical probing (Rauch et al., 2026); attention gating is directly adopted from LLMs (Qiu et al., 2025); and using an expressive ViT decoder follows findings from vision MAE (He et al., 2022).

Complexity and parameter count of the probe: As shown in Table 10, CGP requires 10,000 prototypes resulting in 23.49M trainable parameters on AudioSet (compared to 0.41M for standard linear probing). While the backbone remains frozen, treating a module with tens of millions of trainable parameters as a pure 'probing' tool borders on parameter-efficient transfer learning / lightweight adaptation.

Gap with prior reported finetuning numbers: While the authors present a credible case that prior reported SOTA numbers (e.g., 50.2 mAP for SSLAM on AS-2M) suffer from reproducibility issues and sensitive optimization heuristics, BAT's finetuned result on AS-2M (48.85 mAP) still trails the unverified reported figure, relying primarily on reproduced baselines to claim SOTA.
